entry.description: David L. Hawk wrote the 2020 proceedings paper Socio-technical-natural systems thinking. Its abstract revisits socio-technical concerns through the environmental context of industrial activity and identifies Trist's work as a point of departure.

profile.why_it_matters: Hawk's paper asks what is omitted when a sociotechnical frame treats the natural environment as background rather than as part of the system under consideration.
key_distinctions: Citing or discussing Trist and Ackoff is not evidence of studying under them.
A publication abstract supports the paper's stated concern, not every biographical claim in the report.
historical_lineage: A proposed extension from sociotechnical to socio-technical-natural inquiry.
practice_connections: Test whether an organisational intervention has pushed ecological effects outside its chosen boundary.
common_misreadings: The entry does not present Hawk as a simple conduit from a single Penn lineage.
open_checks: The full paper and primary records for the Penn, Stockholm, and named collaborator claims remain to be reviewed.
